title: Bilge Aft of Frame 55 — Wash, Dry and Corrosion Product Removal
abstract: Wash, dry and mechanical removal of corrosion product from the bilge area aft of frame 55, done before any corrosion inspection or treatment so that the measured material loss is real and not masked by deposit.

sections.purpose: This task prepares the bilge between frame 55 and the rear pressure bulkhead for corrosion inspection or for inhibitor treatment, by removing water, deposit and loose corrosion product without damaging the frame foot radius.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft on the ground and approximately level so that the wash water drains to the low point. The aft cargo compartment lining and the floor panels above the working area must be out. Warm air drying takes several hours and cannot be shortened; plan the task at the start of a shift. Do not use the compartment for any other work while the inhibitor-free surfaces are exposed.
sections.procedure: 1. Get access to the aft cargo compartment through access panels 133CR and 142AR, and open the aft belly fairing at 191CL and 192AR. 2. Remove the insulation blankets from the working area and put them in the drying rack. Do not re-use a blanket that stays wet after drying. 3. Remove the standing water with the vacuum extractor. 4. Wash the area with the approved alkaline agent using the low-pressure lance. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A HIGH-PRESSURE LANCE. IT DRIVES WATER BEHIND THE FRAME FOOT. 5. Rinse with clean water until the run-off is neutral on the test paper. 6. Remove loose corrosion product with a non-metallic scraper and a scotch pad. WARNING: DO NOT USE A WIRE BRUSH OR A ROTARY TOOL ON THE FRAME FOOT RADIUS. THE RADIUS IS FATIGUE CRITICAL. 7. Dry the area with warm air at the temperature and duration given in the standard practice. 8. Check that each drain path is clear by flowing water through it and observing the discharge. 9. Do a visual check of the cleaned area under adequate light and record the position of any deposit that could not be removed. 10. Do not leave the cleaned area untreated for more than 48 hours.
sections.close_out: Install the dried insulation blankets or new blankets as required. Install the floor panels and close the belly fairing if no further work follows. Record the wash, the drying time and the drain path result. If the area is to be inspected, hand over directly to the inspection task without closing the compartment.

safety_precautions: Ventilate the compartment while the cleaning agent is in use.
Use eye and skin protection with the alkaline agent.
Do not use a naked flame or a heat gun near a wet blanket.

title: Bilge Aft of Frame 55 — Wash, Dry and Corrosion Product Removal

issue.reason: A masking step is added for the suppression metering orifice block that now sits inside the sprayed area, with a check that the mask is removed before close-up.

abstract: Wash, dry and mechanical removal of corrosion product from the bilge area aft of frame 55, done before any corrosion inspection or treatment so that the measured material loss is real and not masked by deposit.

sections.purpose: This task prepares the bilge between frame 55 and the rear pressure bulkhead for corrosion inspection or for inhibitor treatment, by removing water, deposit and loose corrosion product without damaging the frame foot radius.
sections.job_setup_note: Do this task with the aircraft on the ground and approximately level so that the wash water drains to the low point. The aft cargo compartment lining and the floor panels above the working area must be out. Warm air drying takes several hours and cannot be shortened; plan the task at the start of a shift. Do not use the compartment for any other work while the inhibitor-free surfaces are exposed. On aircraft at the extended discharge standard, the third stage metering orifice block of the cargo suppression distribution sits inside the wash area in zones 133 and 142. It must be masked before the lance is used: an orifice partly blocked by wash residue or by inhibitor is not visible from outside and changes the flow balance the suppression substantiation depends on.
sections.procedure: 1. Get access to the aft cargo compartment through access panels 133CR and 142AR, and open the aft belly fairing at 191CL and 192AR. 2. Remove the insulation blankets from the working area and put them in the drying rack. Do not re-use a blanket that stays wet after drying. 3. On aircraft at the extended discharge standard, mask the metering orifice block and its two downstream unions with the sealing caps from the tool set, and enter the number of caps fitted on the work card. CAUTION: DO NOT MASK WITH TAPE. ADHESIVE RESIDUE IN A METERING ORIFICE IS AS BAD AS WASH RESIDUE AND IS HARDER TO FIND. 4. Remove the standing water with the vacuum extractor. 5. Wash the area with the approved alkaline agent using the low-pressure lance. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A HIGH-PRESSURE LANCE. IT DRIVES WATER BEHIND THE FRAME FOOT. 6. Rinse with clean water until the run-off is neutral on the test paper. 7. Remove loose corrosion product with a non-metallic scraper and a scotch pad. WARNING: DO NOT USE A WIRE BRUSH OR A ROTARY TOOL ON THE FRAME FOOT RADIUS. THE RADIUS IS FATIGUE CRITICAL. 8. Dry the area with warm air at the temperature and duration given in the standard practice. 9. Remove every sealing cap and check the count against the work card entry. Do not proceed until the numbers agree. 10. Check that each drain path is clear by flowing water through it and observing the discharge. 11. Do a visual check of the cleaned area under adequate light and record the position of any deposit that could not be removed. 12. Do not leave the cleaned area untreated for more than 48 hours.
sections.close_out: Install the dried insulation blankets or new blankets as required. Install the floor panels and close the belly fairing if no further work follows. Record the wash, the drying time, the drain path result and, where the orifice block was masked, the cap count fitted and removed. If the area is to be inspected, hand over directly to the inspection task without closing the compartment.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft, all variants. Steps 3 and 9 apply to aircraft at the extended discharge standard of MOD-134860 only

safety_precautions: Ventilate the compartment while the cleaning agent is in use.
Use eye and skin protection with the alkaline agent.
Count the sealing caps in and out; a cap left in an orifice is undetectable in service.
